line: Lenovo Yoga Pro 9i Aura Edition Gen 10 (16" Intel, 2025)
config_name: Yoga Pro 9i Aura Edition Gen 10 — Core Ultra 7 255H, RTX 5050 8GB, 32GB LPDDR5X, 1TB SSD, 16" 3.2K Tandem OLED 120Hz

specs.keyboard_notes: Yoga creator keyboard, per-key backlight on upper trims; CNET noted slightly awkward keyboard placement

battery.notes: 84Wh (VERIFIED on lenovo.com/ca). RTX 5050 + Tandem OLED; ~8-9h light mixed use, less under GPU load.

price.notes: Lenovo CA hides ld+json price (0) on this PDP; page confirms InStock. CNET as-reviewed US$1,950 (Ultra 9/5050 tier); this Ultra 7 tier estimated ~US$1,850 x 1.35. Lenovo CA runs eCoupon pricing.

reviews.quote: Centered around a gorgeous 16-inch OLED display, this Yoga laptop provides the performance and build that graphics pros demand.
Six-speaker array produces tinny, hollow sound

praises: 3.2K Tandem OLED holds 1,600-nit HDR peaks without dimming like older OLEDs — best 16-inch creator panel near this price
RTX 5050 eases DaVinci Resolve and Premiere exports far beyond what an iGPU-only Slim can do
84Wh battery is unusually large for a thin 16-inch creator clamshell
SD Express slot + HDMI + USB-A means no dongle bag for photography workflows
Aluminium chassis stays rigid; lid flex is minimal for a 16-inch ultrabook
complaints: Six-speaker array sounds tinny and hollow even at mid volume (CNET con, echoed by users on calls)
Keyboard sits close to the front edge — awkward palm position on long typing sessions (CNET con)
RAM is soldered and capped at 64GB with no user upgrade path
Fans audibly spin up during GPU exports in the thin 16-inch chassis
Lenovo.com 'sale' price requires stacking eCoupons; street price at Best Buy CA fluctuates

design_philosophy: Lenovo's 16-inch creator flagship: thin-and-light chassis with discrete RTX graphics, a studio-grade Tandem OLED, and a large battery, aimed at photographers/video editors who want workstation output without a gaming-laptop aesthetic. This Ultra 7 + RTX 5050 tier is the sensible mid-point of that formula.
rating_notes: Ratings anchored on CNET's Editors' Choice review of the sibling Ultra 9 285H + RTX 5050 + 32GB + 1TB config (8.6/10, US$1,950, VERIFIED quotes in NOTES.md).
